newsitem.title: UK: UK oil group "surprised" by Greenpeace application.
newsitem.headline: UK oil group "surprised" by Greenpeace application.

text.p: Britain's offshore oil industry association on Wednesday expressed surprise at an application from environmental lobby group Greenpeace for all new offshore acreage on offer in the UK's latest oil licensing round.
The UK Offshore Operators Association (UKOOA) said it was "surprised to learn that Greenpeace has applied for a licence to manage areas...in the 17th round of oil licensing."
UKOOA said Greenpeace had quoted selectively from British government criteria for applications to explore deep waters on the margin of the Atlantic west of Britain's Shetland islands.
Greenpeace, in its first applications for oil licenses, said earlier it planned to set aside the 22,000 square miles of unexplored territory north of Scotland to protect wildlife.

"Whatever Greenpeace might believe should be the case in the future, life today and the expectations of consumers with regard to living standards, comfort and mobility, depend on the availability of adequate resources of fossil fuels," UKOOA director James May said.
UKOOA represents 34 oil companies licensed to explore for and produce oil and gas in British waters.
